messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: High GPU memory evictions on serving-prod-app-2 during prefill stage. 20% of containers in pool 'hotpool-2' restarted in last 10m. Suspected long-context prefills. Link: https://infra.redwood/alerts/1742500000
oncall-ml: I'm on it. Which model / route is spiking?
eng-runtime: Seeing a surge to 14k token prefill on route /v1/chat/generate -> model: gptx-7b-ql8. KV cache + prefill combined > GPU mem. Logs: `OOM when allocating tensor (requested 1.2 GiB)` on container id 0a3f2b.
sre-lead: Any node flaps? metrics look steady but pods are restarting (OOMKilled) not node-level driver resets.
sam: Customer CS ticket (T-8241) reporting intermittent 500s from us-west2. Could be related.
cs-ops: Confirmed — multiple customers on west cluster saw failed responses starting ~1742499940. We told them we are investigating.
oncall-ml: Quick mitigation plan: 1) throttle max_prefill_tokens to 4096 for the route, 2) push small-model fallback (gptx-3b-ql8) for canary traffic, 3) enable aggressive KV eviction on hotpool-2. I'll run steps 1+2 now.
eng-runtime: Patch ready. small rollout command:
```
kubectl set env deploy/serving-runtime PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=4096 -n serving-prod
kubectl apply -f /manifests/fallback-gptx-3b-canary.yaml
```
I'll enable a transient admission hook to prefer fallback when mem > 75%.
incident-bot: Runbook: Prefill OOM -> https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/prefill-oom. Reminder: use `--eviction=aggressive` on kvcache controller for quick relief.
eng-runtime: Applied PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS to serving-runtime in us-west2. Canary routing active (10%). Observed reduction in OOMs in the canary pods.
sre-lead: Great. Start gradual traffic shift + watch for regression in latency. We should also limit single-request token cap at the API gateway to prevent huge bursts from hitting prefill.
oncall-ml: Gateway limit patch queued: nginx config snippet:
```
location /v1/chat/generate {
  proxy_set_header X-Max-Prefill 4096;
}
```
mia: Running a quick log grep for the container crash stack: `RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory at aten::empty` — consistent with fragmentation + large contiguous alloc on prefill.
cs-ops: Customer-facing update drafted: "We are mitigating an infrastructure memory issue affecting some long-context requests in US-West. Temporary token limits and fallback models are in place; no data loss. We'll update in 30m." Please 👍 or edit.
sam: 👍 looks good. Add estimated mitigation ETA 10-15m.
eng-runtime: Increasing KV eviction aggressiveness now on hotpool-2. Command: `kubectl patch configmap kvcache --patch '{"data":{"eviction":"aggressive"}}'`
incident-bot: Note: autoscaler shows hotpool-2 at 95% util for 5m — consider burst capacity.
sre-lead: Launching a temporary burst node (g4x-large) to reduce pressure while eviction + throttle stabilize. Starting now.
oncall-ml: After canary stability 5m, I'll ramp fallback to 30% and continue monitoring.
eng-runtime: Canary stable at 10m, OOMs down from 20% to 2% of pods. Ramping fallback to 35%.
cs-ops: Customer update sent. First replies trickling in, mostly acknowledgement. No escalations yet.
sre-lead: Added brief oncall handoff note for night rotation: we reduced prefill cap, enabled fallbacks, bumped eviction and spun up burst node. If OOMs return, next steps: 1) cordon hot nodes, 2) force scale hotpool, 3) temporary feature flag to disable long_prefill for free-tier.
oncall-ml: Logging patch to record per-request prefill_token_count for rollout evaluation.
eng-runtime: One pod still restarted 5m ago, root cause appears to be a corner case: single request with 32k prefill tokens from internal load test. I've blackholed that client, sending IP to infra.
mia: Added small tracing snippet to correlate requests -> container: `trace.add_tag('prefill_tokens', N)` to help future triage.
sre-lead: Wrapping up here. Handing off to night-oncall (sam) at 1742500300. Please escalate to oncall-sre if error rate > 5% or more than 3 pods OOM in 15m.
sam: Taking handoff. Summary noted. Will watch through the night and follow the runbook if it reappears.
incident-bot: Incident annotated: priority=high, impact=partial-customer-failure (US-WEST), mitigations=throttle+fallback+kv-evict+burst-node, handoff_to=sam, ticket=T-8241.
cs-ops: Thanks team. I'll close the customer loop once we see 30m of stability.
eng-runtime: Postmortem TODOs: add granularity to kernel allocator diagnostics, revisit fragmentation mitigations, and consider model-level prefetch caps.
sam: Acknowledged. If anyone adds follow-ups, tag me. Good job everyone :thumbsup:
